publication: The Newark Herald (pages 1-12); bound together with The New Jersey Herald News (pages 13-20)
summary: 20-page scan combining two separate Newark, N.J., Black weeklies for the week of July 2, 1938: The Newark Herald (Vol. 11, No. 20, City Edition, 12 pages) and The New Jersey Herald News (Vol. 1, No. 9, 8 pages). Both papers lead with the death of poet/NAACP leader James Weldon Johnson in a Maine auto-train crash, and both cover the Newark embezzlement case against Douglass-Harrison apartment manager Daniel J. Winge and the murder of Marie Boland with her husband John Boland sought as suspect. Remaining pages cover society, church, club, sports (heavy Joe Louis/Max Schmeling aftermath coverage), and NJ community news across Newark, Montclair, Orange, Belleville, Bordentown, Jersey City, Morristown, Bayonne, and shore towns.

incidents.what: James Weldon Johnson killed and his wife Grace Nail Johnson injured when their car was struck by a train at a grade crossing near Wiscasset, Maine; funeral held Thursday, June 30, at Harlem's St. Mark's Church with burial in New York
Newark police issue a warrant and seek arrest of Daniel J. Winge, former Douglass-Harrison apartments assistant manager, for embezzlement of Prudential Insurance Co. funds
Marie Boland, 38, of 6 Rutgers St., Newark, is shot to death in her kitchen; husband John Boland sought for questioning as suspect after being separated from her for three months
Joe Louis knocks out Max Schmeling in the first round at Yankee Stadium; Louis donates $2,500 to the Urban League and NAACP from the fight receipts

Alabama Supreme Court rejects appeal for Scottsboro defendant Clarence Norris, prompting renewed local and national campaign, including a fresh Newark-area committee drive, to save the remaining Scottsboro Boys

connections: This scan bundles two separate NJ Black newspapers from the same week -- The Newark Herald (pages 1-12) and The New Jersey Herald News (pages 13-20) -- both independently covering the James Weldon Johnson death and the Dan Winge embezzlement case, showing overlapping coverage across competing NJ Black weeklies

Newark Herald sports pages extensively cover the Newark Eagles Negro National League baseball club (Effa Manley) and NJ amateur tennis (Elizabeth 'Civil War' rivalry), tying national Black sports press coverage to local NJ teams
Scottsboro Boys defense campaign coverage links Newark-area ministers and NAACP committee members to the national Scottsboro Defense Committee network
